title: Residual unit decomposition of a face-localized monoid chart
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative local ring, let $R,Q$ be fine saturated additive monoids [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and let $h:R\to Q$ induce an isomorphism $h^{\rm gp}$. Let $\alpha:R\to(A,\cdot)$ be a homomorphism, set $G=\alpha^{-1}(A^\times)$, $R_G=\{r-g:r\in R,g\in G\}$, $S=R_G/G^{\rm gp}$. Extend $\alpha$ to the monoid homomorphism $\alpha_G:R_G\to(A,\cdot)$ by $\alpha_G(r-g)=\alpha(r)\alpha(g)^{-1}$. Suppose that $a:S\to(A,\cdot)$ is a monoid homomorphism and $\epsilon:R^{\rm gp}\to A^\times$ is a group homomorphism satisfying $\alpha_G(x)=\epsilon(x)a(\bar x)$ for every $x\in R_G$. Put $C=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[Q]$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], choose a prime $\mathfrak q$ contracting to $\mathfrak m$, and put $B=C_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $F=\{q\in Q:[q]\in B^\times\}$, $Q_F=\{q-f:q\in Q,f\in F\}$, $N=h(G^{\rm gp})$, $P=Q_F/N$, $T=Q_F/F^{\rm gp}$. Monoid rings $E[M]$ consist of finite sums $\sum c_u[u]$ with $[u][v]=[u+v]$.
Then $G,F$ are faces, meaning submonoids with $x+y$ in the submonoid only if both summands belong to it; $h^{-1}(F)=G$, $R_G^\times=G^{\rm gp}$, $Q_F^\times=F^{\rm gp}$, and $S,T$ are sharp (their only invertible element is $0$) fine saturated monoids with finite free group completions. Put $M=Q^{\rm gp}/N\cong S^{\rm gp}$ and $K=F^{\rm gp}/N\subset M$. The group $K$ is finite free, and $P$ is the inverse image of $T$ under $M\to T^{\rm gp}$. There exists a group section $\sigma:T^{\rm gp}\to M$ with $\sigma(T)\subset P$, giving $P\cong K\oplus T$ by $(k,v)\mapsto k+\sigma(v)$. The induced $f:S\to P$ has coordinates $(\delta,\beta)$ with $\beta(s)\ne0$ for every $s\ne0$.
Let $C_F$ mean the localization of $C$ at the multiplicative subset $\{[f]:f\in F\}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], inverting all $[f]$ for $f\in F$. There is an $A$-algebra isomorphism
$$C_F\cong A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[S]}\mathbf Z[K\oplus T],$$
where $\mathbf Z[S]\to A$ sends $[s]$ to $a(s)$ and the other map is induced by $f$. With $\chi=\epsilon\circ(h^{\rm gp})^{-1}$, this isomorphism sends $[q]$ to $\chi(q)[k][v]$ when the class of $q$ in $P$ is $(k,v)$, and $[q]/[f]$ to $\chi(q-f)[k'][v']$ with $(k',v')$ the class of $q-f$. It identifies the chosen localizations and their completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; $q\notin F$ holds exactly when its $T$-coordinate is nonzero. No injectivity of $S^{\rm gp}\to T^{\rm gp}$ is asserted.

source.place: VI 1.6 and VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, printed pp. 70, 98--99; agent-supplied tensor and residual-unit refinement of the formal chart, returned proof Steps 1--4.

proof.text: Products in a commutative ring are units exactly when both factors are units: if $xyu=1$, then $x(yu)=y(xu)=1$. Thus $G$ and $F$ are submonoids and faces. The map $A\to B$ reflects units: if $a\in\mathfrak m$, its image lies in $\mathfrak qB$, the maximal ideal of $B$, so is not a unit; if $a\notin\mathfrak m$, it is a unit already in $A$. Here use the prime-localization description and the local-ring unit criterion. The tensor relation $[h(r)]=\alpha(r)$ therefore gives $h^{-1}(F)=G$. Cross multiplication $r+g'=r'+g$ shows that $\alpha(r)\alpha(g)^{-1}=\alpha(r')\alpha(g')^{-1}$, so the specified extension $\alpha_G$ is well defined.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening] to $(R,G)$ and $(Q,F)$. The faces were proved in Step 1 and both monoids are fs by hypothesis. This gives exactly $R_G^\times=G^{\rm gp}$, $Q_F^\times=F^{\rm gp}$, sharp fs monoids $S,T$, and embeddings $S\subset R^{\rm gp}/G^{\rm gp}$ and $T\subset Q^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp}$ identifying these quotient groups with $S^{\rm gp},T^{\rm gp}$; both groups are finite free. Since $h(G)\subset F$, the subgroup $N=h(G^{\rm gp})$ lies in $F^{\rm gp}$; the isomorphism $h^{\rm gp}$ identifies $M=Q^{\rm gp}/N$ with $S^{\rm gp}$.

source.place: VI 1.6 and VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, printed pp. 70, 98--99; agent-supplied tensor and residual-unit refinement of the formal chart, returned proof Steps 1--4.

proof.text: The quotient $P$ embeds in $M$: two elements $w,w'$ of $Q_F\subset Q^{\rm gp}$ have the same image in $M$ exactly when $w-w'\in N$, precisely its defining quotient relation. It generates $M$, hence $P^{\rm gp}=M$. The quotient $M\to Q^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp}=T^{\rm gp}$ has kernel $K=F^{\rm gp}/N$. Moreover $P$ is the inverse image of $T$: if the image of $m\in M$ is in $T$, choose $w\in Q_F$ with that image. The difference $m-\bar w$ is represented by an element of $F^{\rm gp}\subset Q_F^\times$, so $m\in P$. Conversely every element of $P$ maps into $T$. In particular $P^\times=K$, since $T$ is sharp and all elements of $K$ have both signs in $P$. Thus $P/K=T$, and the group kernel and surjectivity required below have been checked.

source.place: VI 1.6 and VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, printed pp. 70, 98--99; agent-supplied tensor and residual-unit refinement of the formal chart, returned proof Steps 1--4.

proof.text: The identification $M\cong S^{\rm gp}$ makes $K$ a subgroup of a finite free abelian group, so [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free] gives that $K$ is finite free. Apply [lem-trf-group-section-monoid-product] to the surjection $P\to T$. Step 3 supplies integral monoids, group completions $M,T^{\rm gp}$ and kernel $P^\times=K$; Step 2 supplies a finite basis of $T^{\rm gp}$. It gives a group section $\sigma:T^{\rm gp}\to M$ with $\sigma(T)\subset P$ and the inverse monoid maps $(k,v)\mapsto k+\sigma(v)$ and $p\mapsto(p-\sigma(\bar p),\bar p)$. This is the asserted $P\cong K\oplus T$, with the factors interchanged from the cited statement.

source.place: VI 1.6 and VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, printed pp. 70, 98--99; agent-supplied tensor and residual-unit refinement of the formal chart, returned proof Steps 1--4.

proof.text: The map $h$ extends to $R_G\to Q_F$ because $h(G)\subset F$. Modulo $N$ it descends to $f:S\to P$, whose coordinates define $(\delta,\beta)$. To show $\beta(s)=0$ forces $s=0$, write $s=\overline{r-g}$. Vanishing means $h(r-g)\in F^{\rm gp}$, hence $h(r)\in Q\cap F^{\rm gp}$. This intersection is $F$: if $q=f_1-f_2$ with $q\in Q$ and $f_i\in F$, the equality $q+f_2=f_1$ and the face condition imply $q\in F$. Thus $r\in G$ by Step 1, and $s=0$. The same intersection calculation shows, for every $q\in Q$, that its $T$-coordinate is zero exactly when $q\in F$.

source.place: VI 1.6 and VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, printed pp. 70, 98--99; agent-supplied tensor and residual-unit refinement of the formal chart, returned proof Steps 1--4.

proof.text: First use the quotient notation $D=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[S]}\mathbf Z[P]$. The monoid-algebra and algebra-tensor universal properties give its $A$-algebra structure and monomials $[p]$ with $[p][p']=[p+p']$, and the balancing relation $[f(s)]=a(s)$. It is generated by these monomials over $A$, because pure tensors generate and every element of $\mathbf Z[P]$ is an integer sum of monomials. Put $\chi=\epsilon\circ(h^{\rm gp})^{-1}$, a group homomorphism to $A^\times$. All its values below are scalar units in $D$ or $C_F$.

source.place: Tags 00CO (definition-localization), 07BH/07BI (local rings), 00E9 (lemma-characterize-local-ring), 00CV/00CX (section-tensor-product / lemma-tensor-product), 00M9 (section-completion), as applicable; explicit agent calculation of the displayed fractions, balancing and inverse maps.

proof.text: Define $Q\to(D,\cdot)$ by $q\mapsto\chi(q)[\bar q]$. It is multiplicative since $\chi$ and the quotient map are homomorphisms. The monoid-algebra universal property extends it to $\mathbf Z[Q]\to D$. For $r\in R$ its value on $[h(r)]$ is $\epsilon(r)[f(\bar r)]=\epsilon(r)a(\bar r)=\alpha(r)$, so this map is compatible with $\mathbf Z[R]\to A$. The algebra-tensor universal property now gives an $A$-algebra map $C\to D$. If $f_0\in F$, its class belongs to $K=P^\times$, so the image $\chi(f_0)[\bar f_0]$ has inverse $\chi(f_0)^{-1}[-\bar f_0]$. Consequently the map extends to $\Phi:C_F\to D$ by fractions: $c/[f_0]\mapsto\Phi(c)\Phi([f_0])^{-1}$. Cross multiplication in the fraction definition [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] proves independence of representatives and preservation of sums and products. In particular $\Phi([q]/[f_0])=\chi(q-f_0)[\overline{q-f_0}]$.

source.place: Tags 00CO (definition-localization), 07BH/07BI (local rings), 00E9 (lemma-characterize-local-ring), 00CV/00CX (section-tensor-product / lemma-tensor-product), 00M9 (section-completion), as applicable; explicit agent calculation of the displayed fractions, balancing and inverse maps.

proof.text: For $w=q-f_0\in Q_F$ put $z(w)=[q]/[f_0]\in C_F$. This is independent of its monoid fraction representative: equality $q+f'_0=q'+f_0$ gives equality of the corresponding monomial products. It is multiplicative and satisfies $z(h(x))=\alpha_G(x)$ for $x\in R_G$, by the tensor relation and inversion of $\alpha(G)$. For $t\in G^{\rm gp}$ we have $\alpha_G(t)=\epsilon(t)$, since its class in $S$ is zero and $a(0)=1$. Therefore $w\mapsto\chi(w)^{-1}z(w)$ is invariant under addition of $h(t)\in N$: its multiplier is $\epsilon(t)^{-1}\alpha_G(t)=1$. It descends to a multiplicative map $y:P\to C_F$ with $y(\bar w)=\chi(w)^{-1}z(w)$, not depending on the lift $w$.

source.place: VI 1.6 and VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, printed pp. 70, 98--99; agent-supplied tensor and residual-unit refinement of the formal chart, returned proof Steps 1--4.

proof.text: For $s=\bar x\in S$, with $x\in R_G$, the preceding formula gives $y(f(s))=\epsilon(x)^{-1}\alpha_G(x)=a(s)$. Hence the monoid-algebra universal property extends $y$ to a map $\mathbf Z[P]\to C_F$ compatible with $\mathbf Z[S]\to A$. The algebra-tensor universal property gives the $A$-algebra map $\Psi:D\to C_F$ with $\Psi([\bar w])=\chi(w)^{-1}z(w)$. All balancing is accounted for by the displayed identity on $f(s)$; neither flatness nor injectivity of a sharp group map is used.

source.place: Tags 00CO (definition-localization), 07BH/07BI (local rings), 00E9 (lemma-characterize-local-ring), 00CV/00CX (section-tensor-product / lemma-tensor-product), 00M9 (section-completion), as applicable; explicit agent calculation of the displayed fractions, balancing and inverse maps.

proof.text: On each $[\bar w]\in D$ the composite $\Phi\Psi$ is $\chi(w)^{-1}\chi(w)[\bar w]=[\bar w]$, so it is the identity, since these monomials generate $D$ over $A$. On $[q]\in C$, $\Psi\Phi$ gives $\chi(q)\chi(q)^{-1}[q]=[q]$, and it fixes $A$; it therefore fixes $C$ and the inverses of all $[f_0]$, hence is the identity on $C_F$. Use $P\cong K\oplus T$ to reindex monomials in $D$: the maps $[p]\leftrightarrow[k][v]$ preserve multiplication and all coefficient relations, so give $D\cong A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[S]}\mathbf Z[K\oplus T]$. Combining with $\Phi$ gives both formulas in the statement.

source.place: VI 1.6 and VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, printed pp. 70, 98--99; agent-supplied tensor and residual-unit refinement of the formal chart, returned proof Steps 1--4.

proof.text: Every $[f_0]$, $f_0\in F$, lies outside $\mathfrak q$: otherwise its image in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak qB$ could not be a unit. Thus $\mathfrak q_F$ is a prime of $C_F$, and $(C_F)_{\mathfrak q_F}\cong B$. Explicitly fractions over $C_F$ map to $B$ by evaluating their monomial denominators, and the reverse map sends $c/s$ ($s\notin\mathfrak q$) to the same fraction; their composites fix all fractions. The isomorphism $\Phi$ carries $\mathfrak q_F$ to a prime $\mathfrak q_D$ of $D$ and induces inverse fraction maps $(C_F)_{\mathfrak q_F}\cong D_{\mathfrak q_D}$. They identify maximal ideals, hence every power of these ideals and the quotient rings by those powers. Applying them termwise to the compatible sequences defining adic completion gives inverse maps on completions. Finally Step 5 gives the claimed nonzero-$T$-coordinate criterion; it does not imply or require injectivity of $S^{\rm gp}\to T^{\rm gp}$.
